data.description:
## Description

**What**: Pure differ + Mutation dataclass (direction, action, target, payload, provenance) + canonical-manifest serializer (stable ordering + content-addressable hash).
**Why**: Foundation for the stateless reconciler. The differ is the single source of mutation intent — no side-effects, no IO.
**Scope**:
- IN: differ.py, Mutation dataclass, canonical-manifest serializer with stable ordering + content-addressable hash, pure-function discipline
- OUT: Applier dispatch (draft-2), fetcher (draft-3), per-element provenance (draft-9)

## Done Definitions

- Differ is a pure function: same (local_state, jira_state) input produces byte-identical canonical manifest across N invocations ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Mutation dataclass carries (direction in {inbound, outbound}, action in enumerated taxonomy including probe, target, payload, provenance); invalid direction/action combinations raise at construction ← Satisfies: sc-1, sc-2
- Canonical-manifest serializer produces stable ordering (sorted by (direction, action, jira_key or local_id)) and content-addressable hash; unit test asserts hash stability across 100 randomized input permutations ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Differ MUST NOT emit (outbound, create) for any local ticket whose dso_local_id is already present in the fetched Jira working set; instead emits (outbound, update) or no-op. Unit test: local ticket with jira_key=DIG-X and Jira has DIG-X bound to that local id then zero create mutations across N passes. ← Satisfies: sc-1
- Differ surfaces unbindable / inconsistent states (e.g., two Jira issues claiming the same dso_local_id) as explicit Mutation entries with action=conflict or action=probe, not as silent no-ops ← Satisfies: sc-1, sc-2
- Unit tests written and passing for all new logic ← Validates Closure Check: "TDD DoD for code-change stories"

## Considerations

- [Architecture] The Mutation taxonomy defined here is consumed by every downstream applier (draft-2, draft-4, draft-5, draft-6, draft-9). Lock the enum early.
- [Testability] Pure-function discipline enables property-based tests on the manifest invariants.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a reconciler developer, I want a pure differ that produces a canonical Mutation manifest
